                                               DISCLAIMER

Though all the efforts have been made to ensure the accuracy and currency of the content on this report, the
same should not be construed as a statement of law or used for any legal purposes. In case of any ambiguity or
doubts, users are advised to verify/check with the appropriate Government Functionary/Authority and/or other
source(s) and to obtain appropriate professional advice. This Report is based on voluntary uploading of data by
the schools having active UDISE+ code in the academic year 2024-25 (reference year) with cutoff date as on 31st
March 2025. The data is filled in the online designed Data Capture Format (DCF). The UDISE+ code to a
recognized school is allotted by the Central Government based on the recommendation of the respective
State/UT Government where the school is located. The responsibility for the accuracy of the data filled in the
DCFs rests with the concerned Nodal Officers, namely Principal/ Vice-Principal/ Headmaster/ Head Teacher/
Senior most teacher at the school level, Cluster Resource Officer at the cluster level, Block Education Officer for
the block level, District Education Officer at the district level and the State Project Director (SPD), Samagra
Shiksha at the State level. The Ministry of Education, therefore, assumes no responsibility or liability for any
errors or omissions in the data and indicators reported in the document. Inclusion of name of a school in any of
the lists in the portal http://udiseplus.gov.in or any of the reports generated in the portal does not confer the
status of recognition to the school by the Ministry of Education, Govt. of India. Post implementation of NEP
2020, requisite reforms in data collection system have been necessitated and UDISE+ has now completely
aligned with the recommendations of NEP 2020 by shifting focus on individual students instead of school wise
consolidated data collected till 2021-22 and hence data from the year UDISE+ 2024-25 data is not strictly
comparable with reports upto 2021-22 on various educational indicators such as GER, NER, Dropout rate etc.
Similarly, population projections used for generating various educational indicators have been moderated based
on the latest trends of birth rate as recorded by SRS system, saturation reports of UIDAI based on Aadhaar
enrolment and the trends of adjoining States in case of smaller States and UTs. Therefore, educational ratios of
UTs and few smaller States have undergone changes and strictly not comparable with previous year’s figures till
2021-22.

      UNIFIED DISTRICT INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR EDUCATION PLUS (UDISE+) 2024-25

                                            KEY RESULTS – ALL INDIA

1. INTRODUCTION:

1.1.       The Indian school Education System is one of the largest in the world with nearly 14.71 lakh schools,
           more than 1.01 Cr teachers and nearly 24.69 Crore students1from pre-primary to higher secondary
           level from varied socio-economic backgrounds. The system strives to maintain standards and
           uniformity across the country while giving ample scope for the country’s diverse culture and heritage
           to grow and flourish.
1.2.       A robust, upto date and credible information collection mechanism is an essential prerequisite for an
           objective evaluation of the system, based on which specific interventions for improvement can be
           designed.
1.3.       To enable seamless exchange of information, , Department of School Education & Literacy
           (DoSE&L) has developed the “Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+)” from
           the reference year 2018-19. The UDISE+ facilitates online uploading of data at school level with inbuilt
           validation checks and subsequent data verification at the Block, District and State level ensure data
           reliability and timely completion. Effectively, UDISE+ has become truly “one nation one database” in
           the school education sector. By the time of closing UDISE+ 2024-25 data entry, all States /UTs except
           the state of West Bengal are directly feeding data into UDISE+ portal of DoSE&L and West Bengal
           maintains its own MIS and provides bulk data link to UDISE+ portal of DoSE&L.
    1.4.   National Education Policy, 2020 vide Para 3.3 envisaged the concept of achievement of “universal
           participation in school by carefully tracking students, as well as their learning levels, in order to ensure
           that they (a) are enrolled in and attending school and (b) have suitable opportunities to catch up and re-
           enter school in case they have fallen behind or dropped out ignited the need of capturing student wise
           data.
    1.5.   To revolutionize the school data collection mechanism further and align the data to monitor the
           recommendations of NEP, w.e.f., 2022-23, individual student wise data collection has been started
           which will help in tracking of the drop out students and saving to the Govt. by way of accurate number of
           students in the school. This is being done for the first time at the National level.
1.6.       This revitalized UDISE+ ecosystem captures data on more than 60 fields for each student and to maintain
           the uniqueness of the child the Aadhaar details were also collected on the voluntarily basis. However,
           apart from Aadhaar a separate unique educational ID (EID) for every student has also been created in the
           UDISE+ portal to cover each and every child under the ecosystem of UDISE+ across country.

1
Number of schools, teachers and students are from UDISE+ 2024-25. Pre-primary enrolment mentioned in this report excludes
pre-primary enrolment in ECCE centres of Anganwadi and private kindergartens, as these are not a part of UDISE+.

                                                             10
1.7.   Through, unique student and teacher Identity, credentials of individuals (Student /Teacher) in the
       education ecosystem can be established more accurately leading to weeding out of duplicate or ghost
       entries resulting into precise identification of beneficiaries for benefit transfers of Samagra Shiksha
       scheme, PM POSHAN Scheme, National Scholarship scheme etc. can bring significant savings to
       government in future years. Unique student wise data also ensures universal access to affordable
       high-quality education by monitoring students’ attendance, learning outcomes, health parameters etc.
       and their progress at all levels (individual, institution, geographic location, region, State/UTs,
       autonomous body, etc.). This will also help in monitoring individual students from the present system
       of school monitoring and promoting good governance by effective expenditure management.
1.8.   With effect from UDISE+ 2022-23, data fields are completely aligned with the recommendations of
       NEP2020. The present publication relates to UDISE+ data for the reference year 2024-25, the data
       observes some real changes from the previous years as this exercise of maintaining a separate student
       base is totally different, unique and incomparable to 2021-22 or prior years. Individual student wise
       data reflects realistic and more accurate picture of education system which is attempted for the first
       time at the national level a departure from school wise consolidated data till 2021-22 and hence the
       UDISE+ 2024-25 data is not strictly comparable with the previous reports upto 2021-22 on various
       educational indicators like GER, NER, Dropout rates etc. However, 2022-23, 2023-24 & 2024-25 are
       comparable.
2. Some of the salient results at all-India level are given in the following paragraphs. This is followed by
    detailed tables at the all-India and State/UT level for the most used indicators based on the UDISE+ data.
    UDISE+ Reports at https://www.education.gov.in/statistics-new?shs_term_node_tid_depth=394

3. Summary findings of UDISE+ 2024-25

3.1.    School, Students and Teachers:
  3.1.1. NEP 2020 identifies enrolment and attendance of children of school going age as primary goals of
             the schooling system. NEP also recommends achieving universal participation in school by
             carefully tracking of students, as well as their learning levels, in order to ensure that they (a) are
             enrolled in and attending school, and (b) have suitable opportunities to catch up and re-enter school
             in case they have left behind or dropped out. This was possible only through building a unique
             student wise database which also helps in identifying dropout of students. It also helps in
             identifying ghost students and helps in transferring benefits to deserving students resulting into
             savings to government and good governance by way of better expenditure management.
  3.1.2. For the first time at the national level individual student wise data has been collected from all
             recognized schools in the country through UDISE+ since 2022-23. Total of 24.69 Crore students
             are enrolled in the academic year 2024-25. Spread of enrolments for the year 2024-25 for different
             levels of education namely, pre-primary, primary, upper primary, secondary and higher secondary
             are given in Chart 1 below. It may be noted that the pre-primary data contained in the UDISE+
             system does not include the pre-primary enrolment of the Early Childhood Care and Education
             (ECCE) system run by the Ministry of Women and Child Welfare through the Anganwadi Centers
             and standalone pre-primary education centers run by different kindergartens. It covers only the
             enrolment in pre-primary classes of different categories of schools. Further Chart 2 represents the
             percentage distribution of enrolments by social categories.

2.1.3   Recognizing, identifying, and fostering the unique capabilities of each student is possible if we have
        unique data of each of the student. UDISE+ 2024-25 attempted to collect student wise data along
        with Aadhaar number of students on voluntary basis to establish a uniqueness. Overall, more than 22
        crore students voluntarily provided Aadhaar number by 2024-25. The distribution of enrolled
        students who provided Aadhaar number are represented in map 2.1.3. Andhra Pradesh has seeded
        Aadhaar numbers for 99.6% of students, while Andaman and Nicobar Islands has achieved 99.5%
        seeding - both representing the highest levels among all States and UTs, followed by Lakshadweep
        (99.1 %), Puducherry (98.9%), Chandigarh (98.5%), Haryana (98.5%) and Maharashtra (98.1%).
        States with lowest Aadhaar seeding data are Meghalaya (31.9%), Manipur (61.0%) and Nagaland
        (62.6%) with national average of 89.4%.

 2.1.4     State wise distribution of Students and Schools in major states:
         One of the primary goals of the schooling system must be to ensure that children are enrolled in and are
         attending school. The availability of schools, teachers and students enrolled in different states are
         presented in Graph 2.1.4. States such as Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Odisha,
         Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam, J&K, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Meghalaya
         percentage of school available are more than percentage students enrolled implying underutilization of
         available schools leading to suboptimal economy to scale. Where as in States viz., Punjab, West
         Bengal, Haryana, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Delhi, Bihar and Kerala, percentage of available
         schools are significantly less as compared to enrolled students indicating more students per school.

2.1.5     Availability of the right mix of schools at all levels being a supply variable in education system largely
          influences the demand factor. Though a large number of primary schools have been established post
          RTE, the commensurate increase in schools at secondary and higher secondary level have not come
          up. This poses the risk of large-scale dropout of students at the higher classes. Graph 2.1.5, 2.1.6 and
          2.1.7 represents the distribution of schools, students, and teachers across different types of school
          category respectively. West Bengal has 79 % primary schools with 48% students and only 3.5%

2.2 Equity of Students participation: Gender, social category and minority groups.

       2.2.1 Education is the single effective tool for achieving social justice and equality. Inclusive
       and equitable education, an essential goal in its own right is also critical to achieving an
       inclusive and equitable society in which every citizen has the opportunity to dream, thrive,
       and contribute to the nation. The education system must aim to benefit India’s children so
       that no child loses any opportunity to learn and excel because of circumstances of birth or
       background. NEP 2020 also reaffirms that bridging the social category gaps in access,
       participation, and learning outcomes in school education will continue to be one of the major
       goals of all education sector development programs. At the national level, 48.3 % students
       are girls. The Gender Parity Index (GPI) measured as ratio of GER of girls to GER of boys
       stood at above 1 at all level indicating more proportionally higher participation of girls as
       compared to boys. Further, the representation of minorities in total enrolment is more than
       20%. Amongst the minorities 79.1 % are Muslim, 10.2% are Christians, 7.3% are Sikh, 2 %
       are Buddhist, 1.3% are Jains and 0.1% Parsi. Chart 2.2.1 represents State wise distribution of
       students among various social background. At the national level, 27.1% students registered in
       UDISE+ are from General category, 17.8 % from SC, 9.9% from ST, 45.2% are OBC
       category.

         Ratio (PTR). Lesser the PTR number represents teachers able to develop healthy one-on-one mentoring
         relationships and offer insight and help in ways that would be impossible in a larger classroom
         recommended for reaching a PTR ratio of 30:1 at all levels of school education system to have a
         reasonable level of interactive learning and achieving desired level of learning outcomes. Therefore,

2.4 School infrastructure
  2.4.1                                            To ensure decent and pleasant service conditions at schools, NEP recommended for providing
  adequate and safe infrastructure, boundary wall, including working toilets, clean drinking water, clean
  and attractive spaces, electricity, computing devices, internet, libraries, and sports and recreational
  resources become paramount importance. Pleasant school environment tends to promote teachers and
  students, including children of all genders and children with disabilities, receive a safe, inclusive, and
  effective learning environment and are comfortable and inspired to teach and learn in their schools.
  Government has taken various measures in this direction and provides financial assistance to States /UTs
  under Samagra Shiksha Scheme. Chart 2.4.1 presents major infrastructure facilities available in the
  schools at the national level. The details of state wise details of basic infrastructures are presented at table
  2.5 in the succeeding section of this report.

2.5      Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) and Dropout Rate:
 2.5.1           The National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020) identified universal education as a key priority,
                 with several initiatives aimed at transforming the education sector and empowering the nation’s
                 youth. At the heart of the NEP vision to achieve 100% Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) till secondary
                 level by 2030, it is necessary to measure GER. The Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) compares the
                 enrolment in a specific level of education to the population of the age-group which is most age-
                 appropriate for that level of education. For example, the GER of primary is student enrolment in
                 class 1 to 5 expressed as a percentage of population in age group 6-10 years. Similarly, GER of
                 upper primary is enrolment in class 6-8 expressed as a percentage of population in age group 11-13
                 years, and so on. Since changes in GER are usually not much on a year-to-year basis, its movement
                 in the long run is of interest. Chart 2.5.1 to 2.5.4 shows the GER for different levels of education
                 across the States. It may also be noted that GER greater than 100% might indicate presence of over
                 or under age children in a particular level of education, inter State migration etc.

                Concepts and Definitions used in UDISE+
Sl No.   Concept                    Definition (with codes as per UDISE+ DCF, wherever applicable)
         (Abbreviations used)
  1.     Types of schools           The following codes of school management have been considered:
         Government schools         Management                                        Code         Type
                                    Department of Education                           1            State Government
                                    Tribal Welfare Department                         2            State Government
                                    Local Body                                        3            State Government
                                    Other State Government. managed schools           6            State Government
                                    Minority Affairs Department                       89           State Government
                                    Social Welfare Department                         90           State Government
                                    Ministry of Labour                                91           State Government
                                    Kendriya Vidyalaya/ Central School                92           Central Government
                                    Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya                        93           Central Government
                                    Sainik School                                     94           Central Government
                                    Railway School                                    95           Central Government
                                    Central Tibetan School                            96           Central Government
                                    Other Central Government/ PSU Schools             101          Central Government
         Government aided schools   Government Aided – 4
                                    Partially Government Aided - 7
         Private unaided schools    Private Unaided recognized - 5
         Other schools              Unrecognized – 8
                                    Madrasa (recognized by madrasa/ wakf board) – 97,
                                    Madrasa (unrecognized) – 98
                                    Madrasa Aided (Recognized) – 99
                                    Veda Schools/Gurukuls/Pathashalas (Aided/Unaided) - 102
  2.     Gross Enrolment Ratio      Total enrolment in a particular level of school education, regardless of age,
         (GER)                      expressed as a percentage of the Population of the official age-group which
                                    corresponds to the given level of school education in a given school year.
                                    Example:
                                    GER primary = Enrolment in class 1 to 5 ÷ projected population in age group 6-10
                                    years
  3.     Net Enrolment Rate (NER)   Total number of pupils enrolled in a particular level of school education who are of
                                    the corresponding official age group expressed as a percentage of the population of
                                    the official age-group which corresponds to the given level of school education in a
                                    given school year.
                                    Example:
                                    NER primary = Children of age 6-10 years enrolled in class 1 to 5 ÷ projected
                                    population in age group 6-10 years
  4.     Adjusted Net Enrolment     Total number of pupils enrolled either in the corresponding level or a higher level of
         Rate (ANER)                the school education who are of the corresponding official age group expressed as a
                                    percentage of the population of the official age-group which corresponds to the
                                    given level of school education in a given school year.
                                    Example:
                                    ANER primary = Children of age 6-10 years enrolled in primary or higher ÷
                                    projected population in age group 6-10 years
                                    ANER upper primary = Children of age 11-13 years enrolled in upper primary or
                                    higher ÷ projected population in age group 11-13 years
                                    For both NER and ANER, the following identity is maintained:
                                    NER <= ANER <= 100.

                                                           187
  5.   Age Specific Enrolment       Total number of pupils enrolled in any level of school education who are of the
       Rate (ASER)                  corresponding official age group expressed as a percentage of the population of the
                                    official age-group which corresponds to the given level of school education in a
                                    given school year.
                                    Example:
                                    ASER 6-10 years = Children of age 6-10 years enrolled in primary or higher ÷
                                    projected population in age group 6-10 years
                                    ASER 11-13 years = Children of age 11-13 years enrolled in primary/ upper
                                    primary/ secondary/ higher secondary ÷ projected population in age group 11-13
                                    years
                                    …
                                    ASER 16-17 years = Children of age 16-17 years enrolled in primary/ upper
                                    primary/ secondary/ higher secondary ÷ projected population in age group 16-17
                                    years
  6.   Percentage of OBC            Total OBC enrolments expressed as a percentage of the total enrolments
       Enrolments to Total
       Enrolments
  7.   Percentage of all minority   Total of all notified minority communities’ enrolments expressed as a percentage of
       Enrolments to Total          the total enrolment
       Enrolments
  8.   Percentage of Muslim         Total of Muslim minority community enrolment expressed as a percentage of the
       minority Enrolments to       total enrolment
       Total Enrolments
  9.   Promotion Rate               Proportion of pupil from a cohort enrolled in a given level at a given school year
                                    who are enrolled in the next grade in the following school year.

10.    Repetition Rate              Proportion of pupil from a cohort enrolled in a given level at a given school year
                                    who are enrolled in the same grade in the following school year
11.    Dropout Rate                 Proportion of pupil from a cohort enrolled in a given level at a given school year
                                    who are no longer enrolled at any grade in the following school year.
                                    The following identity is maintained while preparing the estimates of promotion
                                    rate, repetition rate and dropout rate:
                                    Each of Promotion Rate, repetition Rate and Dropout Rate is non negative and
                                    Promotion Rate + Repetition Rate + Dropout Rate = 100
12.    Retention Rate               Percentage of a cohort of pupils (or schools) enrolled in a first grade of a given level
                                    of education in a given school year who are expected to reach the last grade of the
                                    level.
13.    Gender Parity Index (GPI)    Ratio of GER of girls to GER of boys. It measures the progress towards gender
       of GER                       parity in education participation and/or learning opportunities available for girls in
                                    relation to those available to boys. It also represents the level of girls’
                                    empowerment in the society.
14.    Pupil Teacher Ratio (PTR)     Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) is the average number of pupils (at a specific level of
                                    education) per teacher (teaching at that level of education) in a given school- year.
15.    AWC                          Anganwadi Centres
